name: Curator
description: Asks an LLM what your library has in common and builds the answers into ordered playlists surfaced as home screen rows.
overview: LLM-inferred vibe categories for your Jellyfin library.

versions.changelog: The weather and time-of-day row no longer announces a clear sky. 'Good for a clear evening' says barely more than 'Good for an evening', so a plain clear sky is left out and the hour carries the title; a clear sky with heat or cold is still named, because a cold bright morning is a specific thing. Every other condition — rain, snow, storm, fog, overcast, hot, cold — is named as before. Titles bought under the old wording are replaced on the next hourly refresh.

The weather and time-of-day home screen row now says plainly what it is for — 'Good for an overcast afternoon' rather than 'Slate Sky Slow Burns'. Titles name the sky and the hour in ordinary words, in sentence case, and vary how they open so they do not all begin the same way. Titles bought under the old wording are replaced automatically on the next hourly refresh rather than lingering for a year.

Each viewer can now get a films-only and a television-only recommendation playlist beside the combined one, switched on with 'Also build a films-only and a television-only list' on the Home screen tab. Both are cut from the same ranking, so they cost no extra model call — even with model-chosen ordering on, it is still one call per viewer. The combined list is always built and unchanged, which is what the Media Bar plugin wants: it takes a single playlist name and separates films from television itself. Note these cannot appear on the Movies and Shows Suggestions tabs — those come from the server's own recommendation endpoints, which no plugin can add to.

Settings page: the tabs now match the Concierge plugin's — text with an underline instead of eight raised pills competing with the Save button beneath them — and the model configurator puts the profile picker and its buttons on one line, with every per-profile setting inside a box of its own so it is clear which settings belong to the selected profile and which do not. Fixes the Runs tab losing its scope highlight when you switch tabs, and stops two startup refreshes buying the same context row titles twice.

A thin context row is now topped up with things suiting the hour either side — evening reaches late night and afternoon, never morning — placed below every genuine match, and only when the row would otherwise look sparse. A row that already has enough is left strictly alone, so a well-stocked evening is never diluted to rescue a starved morning. Measured on a real library, a cloudy morning went from 1 matching item to 39 while a rainy evening kept all 106 and gained nothing. The classification prompt also stops holding weather and time of day to the same bar: weather stays sparing, but most items should now carry a time of day, and the prompt names the trap of calling everything an evening film. That half applies to items classified from now on — an existing library needs Re-condense everything to benefit. Also from 0.8.3.0: the weather and time-of-day rows became ONE row for the moment you are in, titled for the pair such as "Rainy Night Cozy Vibes", graded rather than strict so it draws in any conditions, one per viewer when each has their own location. And from 0.8.2.0: full-width settings tabs, a scrollable A-to-Z summaries list with Weather and When columns, and Save at the top of each tab.
